transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-18
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Olivia Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Riley Torres (Redwood CSM), Aisha Khan (CTO - Veridian Labs), Ben Morales (Infra), Sofia Ruiz (Security), Marco Li (SRE)

Summary (auto): quick sync on pilot telemetry, egress shaping trial, kernel rollforward schedule; flagged a transient latency spike tied to egress routing; agreed to run controlled egress shaping and push kernel change to canary nodes.

Topics: pilot status, egress shaping plan, fallback routing behavior, kernel rollforward, telemetry gaps, compliance ask, next steps

00:00 Olivia: Okay hey everyone thanks for joining, we just wanted a short weekly sync to cover the egress shaping experiments and the kernel rollforward plan. Are we good on time, Riley?
00:12 Riley: Yep should be about 45, 50 minutes depending, mostly checkpoints.
00:18 Aisha: Great, yes thanks, want to make sure we get to the latency spike we saw last Thursday.
00:26 Marcus: Quick preface, we pushed the profiling patch to canary nodes last night, it's instrumented to capture per-route tail latency and KV cache hits. Note: the log key says KV cash in places so ignore that ;).
00:44 Ben: ha yeah we noticed the kv cash typo in the logs, we thought at first it was the k-v cache.
00:52 Marcus: Right, it's just a 1-line thing, not affecting measures.
01:05 Olivia: Okay can we run through results first? Ben, can you summarize what you saw in the last 72 hours?
01:12 Ben: Sure, so baseline before Friday was stable: p50 ~85 ms, p95 ~210, p99 ~480. After the rollout to pooled nodes we saw intermittent p95 jumps to 400-700ms primarily during egress periods when requests route to the cross-region fallback. It aligns with our egress throttle kicking in, so it looks routing->egress shaping->latency compound.
01:42 Aisha: Is that the same fallback rule we configured to prefer local region then fall back to central?
01:48 Marcus: Yeah, the policy is region-pref then fallback to central, with cost-tier fallback enabled. The compounding issue seems to be that when the central egress path is saturated, the requests are queued and our batching increases which pushes p99 up. There's also a small artifact where quanti zation fallback causes more CPU on those nodes.
02:12 Sofia: For security, any of the fallback traffic touching third-party egress points is logged and encrypted but we need the exact egress IP list for audit.
02:23 Olivia: We'll provide the IP list. Marcus will also attach the telemetry export we used.
02:30 Marcus: Yes I'll upload the telemetry csv and a short explainer. Keep in mind some field names are messy — e.g., 'kernel_ver' sometimes blank on older canaries.
02:46 Marco: On canaries we saw kernel 1.14.2 for most but a handful running 1.13.x which may explain a slight perf delta.
02:56 Ben: Right, and the 1.13 nodes showed worse KV hit ratios under burst.
03:05 Olivia: All right so two parallel actions: the egress shaping test to control traffic into central egress and a kernel rollforward to standardize nodes. Marcus, what's the rollforward plan?
03:15 Marcus: Plan A: roll kernel 1.14.3 to 10% canaries, monitor 24hr, then 50% if stable, full within 72 hours. The build includes a threading fix that reduces GC spikes under heavy batching. We'll provide a rollback tag. Note: the patch touches our Numa settings so ops should watch allocs.
03:40 Ben: Any changes to ABI or model loading? We don't want restart storms during business hours.
03:46 Marcus: No ABI changes, it's binary-level opt; it requires a single process restart per node. We'll schedule canary during off-peak windows.
03:55 Aisha: Good. For egress shaping, can we do a phased shaping where we limit central egress to X rps and reroute overflow to regional?
04:05 Olivia: That's what Ben proposed in the doc — a headroom cap with weighted routing to prefer regionals.
04:12 Ben: Yeah, I'd like to run three shaped windows: 1) 10am-12pm local replicant test, 2) highest traffic window emulation, and 3) long-run overnight. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 and batch sizes.
04:30 Riley: For pilot success criteria let's re-state: decrease p99 spikes by 30% during overflow windows and no more than 5% throughput loss.
04:40 Aisha: That sounds right. Also must preserve audit trail for any routed-to-central requests.
04:47 Sofia: On the compliance front, we'll need KMS key IDs for the canary egress and proof of zero-data-retention on the intermediate proxies.
04:56 Olivia: We'll include that in the packet. Marcus, you flagged a telemetry gap earlier?
05:02 Marcus: Yes, a couple things: 1) per-token timing isn't exported for some older runtime variants, 2) tracing sampling was at 5% and missed a few bad flows, and 3) the agent sometimes strips the 'route_hint' field due to a parsing bug. Those are fixable but we should capture them in the runbook.
05:30 Ben: We bumped tracing to 20% last night which captured the pattern; I'll attach the traces.
05:36 Olivia: Great. Any external vendor risk — competitors or infra — we should mention?
05:40 Aisha: We're also evaluating Bedrock for a comparison pilot but it's mostly for pricing. No immediate switch.
05:46 Marcus: Noted. We did a quick throughput comp vs Anthropic last quarter, but that's separate.
05:52 Marco: Back to the kernel rollforward — how will canaries be selected? Random or sticky to current problematic nodes?
05:59 Marcus: We'll seed canaries on nodes with lowest load but also include a replica of one problematic node to validate fix under stress. Should avoid rolling the oldest nodes first.
06:12 Ben: On measurement, we'll look at KV hit rate, batch sizes, CPU steal, and per-route tail latency. Also watch for timeouts upstream.
06:25 Aisha: One more ask — can Redwood provide a concise RPO/RTO note tied to the rollback plan? We'll need to include that in our change advisory board.
06:36 Riley: Yes, we can create a CAB-ready note. I'll draft it.
06:40 Sofia: Also want confirmation that no logs or request payloads are sent to Redwood-hosted analytics; our legal team still needs that assurance.
06:48 Olivia: We only collect telemetry and traces you opt-in; payloads are never stored unless explicitly enabled. We'll provide the legal blurb.
06:55 Marcus: Quick note on the fallback routing: the current algorithm does a cost-tier selection, but when cookies or session affinity are present it can cause uneven distribution which exacerbates queueing. Might need to temporarily disable affinity during the test.
07:18 Ben: Good call, we can do a no-affinity window for 30 minutes to see distribution effects.
07:25 Aisha: Fine with that as long as we inform product.
07:30 Olivia: OK we'll put a communication plan together.
07:35 Marcus: I'll also include a small synthetic load script that mimics your real traffic profile so you can run local tests before we hit production canaries.
07:46 Marco: That would help. Please include the seed files.
07:52 Marcus: Will do.
08:00 Olivia: Anything else on telemetry or compliance?
08:05 Sofia: For the KMS IDs, can you also note whether keys are customer-managed or Redwood-managed for the canary? We need customer-managed for the pilot.
08:14 Olivia: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS for Private pilots; we'll provide steps to configure and rotate.
08:20 Ben: On egress IP list, we'll want the expected CIDR blocks and any dynamic ranges.
08:26 Marcus: We'll export the static ranges and note dynamic ranges used only in failover.
08:32 Riley: Recap of next steps: Olivia sends spreadsheet, Marcus pushes patch & runbook, Ben runs egress shaping tests, Sofia posts compliance checklist.
08:45 Aisha: Good. Also I'd like a short executive summary for our board by Monday.
08:50 Olivia: We'll prepare one.
08:56 Ben: Quick question — if the kernel rollforward doesn't reduce p99 by target, what is fallback? Full rollback? Alternative tuning?
09:06 Marcus: If canary fails, we rollback the canary nodes immediately, and then either increase headroom on egress or apply a micro-patch that reduces batching aggressiveness. We'll treat rollback as default safe plan.
09:18 Marco: Sounds good.
09:22 Olivia: All right, unless there are any blockers, we'll proceed. Any final items?
09:28 Sofia: Just please tag the compliance docs in the pilot channel so legal can pick up.
09:34 Olivia: Will do. Thanks everyone.
09:38 Meeting ends.

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription sometimes merged words (e.g., "quanti zation"), speaker labels occasionally generic — cleaned minimally.
